Quantile mapping best mitigates p-tau217 assay effects

Across 330 participants measured on four p-tau217 platforms per cohort, quantile normalization or mapping most reduced assay effects, while conditional quantile mapping performed best across cohorts; the methods are for research harmonization, not clinical result conversion.

Key quantitative results: Raw assay correlations were strong in ADNI (Spearman r=0.81–0.89) but weaker in HCP, at 0.46–0.66 among commercial assays and 0.37 for the in-house assay.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217Amyloid PET CentiloidAssay harmonization

Added October 28, 2026 · DOI:10.1002/dad2.70518; PMID:42921107; PMCID:PMC13691630

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Cross-platform p-tau217 values remained materially different despite strong correlations. Quantile normalization and mapping best reduced within-cohort assay effects, and conditional quantile mapping best handled pooled cohort effects. Z-scores and CentiMarker had little benefit in these data. The findings support research integration choices but should not be used to translate an individual patient's result across assays.

Study design

The study used repeated p-tau217 measurements in ADNI (n=219) and the Human Connectome Project (n=111), with four platforms per cohort. It compared mean adjustment, Z-score approaches, CentiMarker, quantile normalization and mapping, conditional quantile mapping, inverse-probability weighting, and marginal standardization. Amyloid positivity used PET Centiloid at least 20.

Key quantitative results

  • Raw assay correlations were strong in ADNI (Spearman r=0.81–0.89) but weaker in HCP, at 0.46–0.66 among commercial assays and 0.37 for the in-house assay.
  • Raw distribution divergence measured by Anderson-Darling A-k-squared was 447.62 in ADNI and 229.40 in HCP.
  • Quantile normalization reduced A-k-squared to 0.03 in ADNI and 0.15 in HCP and reduced within-subject variability from 0.196 to 0.174 and from 0.682 to 0.589, respectively.
  • Quantile mapping reduced A-k-squared to 0.08 in ADNI and 0.27 in HCP; its HCP within-subject variability of 0.563 was the lowest reported there.
  • Conditional quantile mapping performed best for pooled multicohort analyses and was the only approach that improved AUC across all assays, although gains were modest; CentiMarker and reference-based Z-scores had minimal impact.

What changed

The paper provides a head-to-head methods benchmark for combining p-tau217 data across assays and cohorts, favoring quantile mapping over common Z-score and CentiMarker approaches in these datasets.

Strength of evidence

Moderate methods evidence from two cohorts with within-person measurements across multiple platforms and several quantitative performance metrics. Generalizability is constrained by cohort selection, assay-specific missingness, reference choice, absence of external prospective validation, and no clinical decision endpoint.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

The study should not be used to convert or reinterpret an individual patient's p-tau217 result. Its immediate value is in research datasets and multisite analyses where assay and cohort effects can otherwise masquerade as biology.

Field medical relevance

Directly addresses assay comparability, statistical harmonization, pooled-cohort analyses, reference dependence, and the boundary between research standardization and clinical laboratory traceability.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The same participants were measured across four platforms within each cohort, allowing direct estimation of assay effects. The proposed transformations improve group-level research comparability but do not establish traceability, calibrator equivalence, or a patient-level conversion equation for clinical reporting.

Access or reimbursement relevance

Research harmonization may improve reuse of multicenter data, but it creates no immediate assay availability, authorization, reimbursement, or coverage pathway.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Can a quantile-mapped value replace an assay's clinical cutoff?
No. The methods harmonize research distributions and do not establish a validated patient-level conversion or authorized cutoff.
Did strong correlations eliminate assay differences?
No. Raw distributions still diverged substantially, and correlations were much weaker in HCP than ADNI.
Which method performed best?
Quantile normalization or mapping best mitigated within-cohort assay effects, while conditional quantile mapping performed best for pooled multicohort data.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Research cohorts rather than routine clinical populations
  • 172 ADNI participants were excluded because C2N values were below quantification or outside calibration
  • No external prospective validation cohort
  • Results depend on reference assay and cohort choice
  • No multiplicity correction
  • Unmeasured factors such as renal function may contribute to cohort effects
  • No clinical traceability or patient-level conversion validation

Primary source · DOI

Zhang VZ, Ferreira PCL, Dong Y, et al. Evaluation of harmonization methods to mitigate assay and cohort effects in plasma p-tau217. Alzheimers Dement (Amst). 2026;18(4):e70518. doi:10.1002/dad2.70518.
